readings.what: the Williamson payloads carry no address and no coordinate at all
readings.literal: baseFacts {apn R483884, landUse null, acreage null, situsAddress null}; zoning {district SF2, jurisdictionKey round-rock-tx}; a 4/4-axis table 20/5/20/20; facetCoverage {baseFacts true, landUse false, acreage false, zoning true, envelope true}. A full-text search of the body for lat/lng/queryPoint/centroid returns NOTHING - the single 'centroid' occurrence is inside another fact's absence REASON prose, not a coordinate, and no geometry field exists. So the draw route cannot be called at all and the card can show no address.
readings.consequence: the defect XD-7's named population is real and this instrument can now reach it; the bucket verdict for these is UNMEASURED (its map leg could not be completed), while the ledger records XD-7 OPEN - which is why the close reports BOTH numbers rather than either alone

readings.what: an address absence that carries no basis, in a payload that declares a sibling absence properly
readings.literal: baseFacts.situsAddress is a BARE NULL (no verdict, no authority, no scope), while baseFacts.situsCity in the SAME object is a full absent-verified declaration naming its authority (Bastrop County CAD roll as published in the conformant-v1 cad-parcel-roll claim), its scopeSearched and the declared vintage - and the payload carries acreage 15433 sqft by shoelace-wgs84, so the parcel has geometry, a district (SF-1) and a 4/4-axis table 30/10/30/20
readings.consequence: the extractor was collapsing a DECLARED absence into the same null as an undeclared one, which is exactly the distinction AGENT_CONTRACT section 5 protects ('an empty result is not an absence ... every absence carries its basis'). Fixed: the payload's declared-absence shape is now read, and a SITUS-ABSENT-UNDECLARED finding names the inconsistency

twoGraderDefectsFoundByMeasurementAndFix.why: Both were found by running the grader against LIVE payloads and reading what it said, not by reviewing it. Both are recorded because a grader that cannot fire on its own named population, or that overclaims in its own basis string, is the defect class this program exists to catch - and because the close quotes these strings.

defect1_xd7_could_not_fire.what: XD-7 is literally 'Williamson: no composed address on the map payload', but its grader returned UNMEASURED whenever the payload carried no situs - i.e. it was structurally blind to the very population it names, because the Williamson payloads carry no situs at all. The defect ledger therefore read XD-7 CLOSED while the condition was in front of it.
defect1_xd7_could_not_fire.fix: the grader now distinguishes an EMPTY read from an ANSWERING read: a payload serving a district, a table or a jurisdiction is answering ABOUT a parcel, and serving it with no composed address is the defect; a payload carrying nothing to be addressed stays UNMEASURED.
defect1_xd7_could_not_fire.provenBy: self-test cases in both directions - FIRES on the Williamson shape, FIRES on the Bastrop shape, UNMEASURED on a wholly empty read, PASSES where a composed address is served

defect2_xd7_basis_overclaimed.what: the first fix's FAIL basis said the payload had 'no address of any kind: no situs, no composed address and no coordinate'. False for the Bastrop parcels: 48021:51735 carries no address but DOES carry a record point (30.10219, -97.30069) and drew 6 vertices from it.
defect2_xd7_basis_overclaimed.fix: the basis now names exactly which of {situs, composed address, coordinate} is absent and which is present.
defect2_xd7_basis_overclaimed.provenBy: a self-test asserting the Bastrop shape's basis contains 'present: a coordinate' and NOT 'no coordinate', plus its complement for a payload with no point.
